    The Agentic QE Framework

    Quality Engineering infused with agentic principles (PACT), balancing classic QE practices with agent orchestration.

    V3 Architecture|12 DDD Bounded Contexts | 51 Agents | 61 Skills

    Executive Summary

    Quality Engineering is evolving. While classical practices remain essential, the emergence of AI agents demands a new orchestration model. The Agentic QE Framework bridges this gap through PACT principles—creating quality systems that augment human expertise rather than replace it.

    Core Definition

    Agentic Quality Engineering = Quality Engineering infused with agentic principles (PACT), balancing classic QE practices with agent orchestration.

    - From testing-as-activity to agents-as-orchestrators
    - From verification theatre to trusted, explainable flows

    V3 Multi-Layer Architecture

    MCP Layer: 25+ tools with connection pooling (0.6ms P95)
    Domain Layer: 12 DDD bounded contexts with lazy loading
    Coordination Layer: Queen Coordinator, consensus, work stealing
    Kernel Layer: Microkernel, plugins, HNSW memory

    PACT Principles in Detail

    P

    Proactive

    Anticipate and prevent failures before they occur

    • Mutation testing to validate test quality
    • Fault injection for resilience testing
    • Risk prediction using historical data
    • Preventive quality gates and automated alerts
    A

    Autonomous

    Self-executing test flows without human intervention

    • Self-healing tests that adapt to UI changes
    • Auto-generated test scenarios from requirements
    • Continuous validation in production
    • Autonomous root cause analysis
    C

    Collaborative

    Human-agent orchestration for optimal outcomes

    • Explainable AI decisions and reasoning
    • Human oversight and approval workflows
    • Shared learning between humans and agents
    • Transparent audit trails for all actions
    T

    Targeted

    Context-driven optimization for specific goals

    • Risk-based testing prioritization
    • Smart resource allocation
    • Context-aware test selection
    • Goal-oriented optimization metrics

      QE Agent Catalog

      51 specialized quality engineering agents across 12 V3 domains, featuring Queen-led orchestration, TDD specialists, and neural learning.

      51Total Agents
      12V3 Domains
      4PACT Principles

      Test Architect

      Strategic AI-powered test design with comprehensive test planning and architecture decisions

      KEY CAPABILITIES

      • AI-powered test strategy design and planning
      • Test architecture decisions and framework selection
      • Test pyramid optimization (unit/integration/E2E ratios)

      TDD Specialist

      TDD methodology expert coordinating Red-Green-Refactor cycles with London/Chicago school support

      KEY CAPABILITIES

      • Coordinate complete TDD Red-Green-Refactor cycles
      • London school (mockist) TDD guidance
      • Chicago school (classicist) TDD guidance

      TDD Red (Write Tests)

      TDD RED phase specialist that writes failing tests defining expected behavior before implementation

      KEY CAPABILITIES

      • Generate comprehensive failing tests from requirements
      • Property-based test generation
      • Edge case identification and test creation

      TDD Green (Make Pass)

      TDD GREEN phase specialist that implements minimal code to make tests pass

      KEY CAPABILITIES

      • Implement code to satisfy failing tests
      • Minimal viable implementation strategy
      • Test-driven code generation

      TDD Refactor (Improve)

      TDD REFACTOR phase specialist that improves code quality while maintaining passing tests

      KEY CAPABILITIES

      • Code quality improvement and optimization
      • Refactoring without breaking tests
      • Design pattern application

      Property Tester

      Property-based testing specialist with automatic input generation and invariant discovery

      KEY CAPABILITIES

      • Property-based test generation (fast-check, jsverify)
      • Automatic property discovery from code analysis
      • Shrinking algorithms for minimal failing cases

      Test Idea Rewriter

      Transform passive test descriptions into active, observable test actions by eliminating "Verify" patterns

      KEY CAPABILITIES

      • Detect and eliminate passive "Verify X" patterns via regex
      • Transform to action-verb-based test descriptions (Click, Type, Submit, Measure, Assert)
      • Process HTML, JSON, and Markdown assessment files

      Parallel Executor

      Distributed parallel execution with sharding, worker pools, and optimal resource utilization

      KEY CAPABILITIES

      • Test sharding across multiple workers
      • Worker pool management and scaling
      • Optimal test distribution algorithms

      Flaky Test Hunter

      Statistical flaky test detection with ML patterns, root cause analysis, and auto-stabilization

      KEY CAPABILITIES

      • Statistical flaky test detection (95% confidence)
      • Pattern analysis (timing, network, state, resource)
      • Automatic stabilization with retry and wait strategies

      Retry Handler

      Intelligent retry logic with exponential backoff, circuit breakers, and failure categorization

      KEY CAPABILITIES

      • Intelligent retry with exponential backoff
      • Circuit breaker pattern for persistent failures
      • Failure categorization (transient vs permanent)

      Integration Tester

      Component integration testing with API contract validation and end-to-end workflow verification

      KEY CAPABILITIES

      • Component integration testing
      • API contract validation
      • Database integration testing

      Coverage Specialist

      O(log n) sublinear coverage analysis with HNSW-indexed gap detection and optimization

      • Smart test prioritization for maximum coverage gain

      Ready to Deploy Your QE Fleet?

      Initialize your agent fleet and start autonomous quality engineering in minutes

      How It Works:

      1. Install Claude Code (CLI or VS Code extension) - your execution environment
      2. Install Agentic QE with npm - provides agent configurations and fleet management
      3. Initialize fleet with aqe init - creates agent files in .claude/agents/
      4. Execute agents via Claude Code's Task tool - agents run autonomously with AI capabilities
      💡 Key Concept: AQE provides specialized agent templates; Claude Code provides the AI execution environment

        Getting Started with Agentic QE

        Your practical guide to beginning the journey from classical to agentic quality engineering with 51 specialized agents, 61 QE skills, and 12 V3 domains at your disposal.

        Before You Begin

        Let me save you three months of pain: Don't start with the agents.

        I know, I know. You're here for the AI stuff. But trust me—I tried jumping straight to agents. Twice. Both times ended with me apologizing to my team and rolling everything back.

        Classical QE Foundation

        Team Readiness

        Technical Foundation

        Missing some? Start there. Seriously. Agents amplify what exists—they don't fix what's broken.

        Your First 30 Days

        Week 1: Baseline and Learn

        Days 1-3: Foundation

        Morning:
        • Take the PACT assessment (honestly)
        • Document current pain points
        • Identify ONE problem to solve
        Afternoon:
        • Set up measurement baseline
        • Define success metrics
        • Share plan with team

        Days 4-5: Education

        Focus: Education
        Actions:
        • Read the Framework documentation
        • Watch 2-3 implementation talks
        • Join the Agentic QE community
        Avoid:
        • Buying tools yet
        • Making big announcements
        • Promising specific outcomes

        Week 2: First Agent Experiment

        Required: Claude Code Installation

        AQE agents execute through Claude Code - the AI-powered CLI and VS Code extension. You must install Claude Code before using Agentic QE.

        Option 1:
        Claude Code CLI
        Download from claude.ai/code
        Option 2:
        VS Code Extension
        Install from VS Code Marketplace
        💡 Claude Code provides the execution environment where AQE agents run via the Task tool

        Install Agentic QE Fleet

        # Option 1: Global Installation (Recommended)
        npm install -g agentic-qe
        # Verify installation
        aqe --version
        # Option 2: Project Installation (Use npx)
        npm install --save-dev agentic-qe
        # Use with npx
        npx aqe init
        System Requirements: Node.js 18+, npm 8+, Claude Code (installed above)

        Your First Agent: qe-test-generator

        Always start with assistance, not automation

        # Initialize AQE Fleet and spawn test generator agent
        aqe init --topology mesh
        aqe test src/components/Button.tsx --coverage 90
        # Or use with Claude Code:
        claude "Generate comprehensive tests for Button component"
        Agent: qe-test-generator
        Capabilities: AI-powered test creation with property-based testing
        Scope: One feature, one developer
        Duration: 1 week experiment
        Configuration: Located in .claude/agents/qe-test-generator/
        Fallback: Can disable instantly
        📖 View full qe-test-generator agent details →
        Real Results from Production Deployment:
        • • Test generation time: 2-3 days → 4-6 hours (60% faster)
        • • Edge case coverage: 45% → 92% (47pp improvement)
        • • Test consistency: Standardized patterns across team
        • • Agent learning: 23% improvement over 3 months

        Week 3: Add a Second Agent

        Introduce: qe-flaky-test-hunter

        Now that test generation is working, tackle flaky tests that plague CI/CD pipelines

        # Spawn flaky test hunter agent
        aqe agent spawn --name qe-flaky-test-hunter
        aqe agent execute --name qe-flaky-test-hunter \
        --task "Analyze test suite for flaky tests"
        Agent Coordination Example:
        1. qe-test-generator creates new tests
        2. qe-test-executor runs tests in parallel
        3. qe-flaky-test-hunter analyzes failures
        4. Agents share results via event bus
        5. qe-flaky-test-hunter auto-fixes detected issues
        📖 View all available agents →
        Results from Case Study (15K test suite):
        • • Flaky test rate: 8-12% → 0.3% (96% reduction)
        • • Investigation time: 4-6 hrs/week → 15 min/week
        • • Auto-fix success: 89% stabilized automatically
        • • CI/CD reliability: 92% → 99.7%

        Week 3 Decision Point

        If Week 2 showed improvement:
        • Add second agent (flaky-test-hunter)
        • Expand to 2 more team members
        • Document agent coordination patterns
        If Week 2 had mixed results:
        • Continue with single agent
        • Adjust configuration based on feedback
        • Seek external guidance

        Week 4: Establish Patterns

        Working Rhythm:
        • Monday: Review agent findings
        • Wednesday: Adjust configurations
        • Friday: Measure and share results
        Feedback Loop:
        • Daily: Quick wins and blockers
        • Weekly: Metrics and adjustments
        • Monthly: Strategic review

        Choose Your Path

        Based on your context, pick ONE path to start:

        Path A: The Debugger's Route

        Start with: Production intelligence and incident analysis
        Best for: Teams drowning in production issues
        Agents:
        qe-production-intelligence
        Capabilities: Learns from production incidents and replays failures
        4-Week Plan:
        • Week 1: Baseline your debugging time and MTTR
        • Week 2: Deploy qe-production-intelligence agent
        • Week 3: Enable incident replay and root cause analysis
        • Week 4: Measure MTTR improvement and pattern learning
        📖 View agent details and configuration →

        Path B: The Tester's Route

        Start with: Test generation and coverage optimization
        Best for: Teams with low test coverage (<40%)
        Agents:
        qe-test-generator
        qe-coverage-analyzer
        Capabilities: AI-powered test creation + O(log n) coverage gap detection
        4-Week Plan:
        • Week 1: Audit current coverage (baseline)
        • Week 2: Deploy qe-test-generator for new tests
        • Week 3: Add qe-coverage-analyzer for gap detection
        • Week 4: Measure coverage increase and test quality
        📖 View agent details and configuration →

        Path C: The Guardian's Route

        Start with: Resilience testing and deployment readiness
        Best for: Teams with stable systems needing better production confidence
        Agents:
        qe-chaos-engineer
        qe-deployment-readiness
        Capabilities: Controlled fault injection + risk-based deployment validation
        4-Week Plan:
        • Week 1: Baseline system resilience metrics
        • Week 2: Deploy qe-chaos-engineer for fault testing
        • Week 3: Add qe-deployment-readiness for go/no-go decisions
        • Week 4: Measure incident reduction and deployment confidence
        📖 View agent details and configuration →

        Path D: The Workflow Automator's Route

        Start with: n8n workflow testing and automation validation
        Best for: Teams using n8n or similar workflow automation platforms
        Agents:
        n8n-workflow-executor
        n8n-trigger-test
        n8n-security-auditor
        Capabilities: 15 specialized agents for comprehensive workflow testing
        4-Week Plan:
        • Week 1: Audit existing n8n workflows and identify critical paths
        • Week 2: Deploy n8n-trigger-test and n8n-node-validator
        • Week 3: Add n8n-security-auditor for credential/compliance checks
        • Week 4: Integrate n8n-ci-orchestrator into deployment pipeline
        📖 View agent details and configuration →

        Path E: The Accessibility Champion's Route

        Start with: WCAG compliance and inclusive quality
        Best for: Teams requiring ADA/Section 508 compliance or serving diverse users
        Agents:
        a11y-ally
        qx-partner
        Capabilities: Accessibility testing + QA-UX collaboration for inclusive quality
        4-Week Plan:
        • Week 1: Baseline current accessibility compliance status
        • Week 2: Deploy a11y-ally for WCAG 2.2 validation
        • Week 3: Add qx-partner for user journey quality analysis
        • Week 4: Measure compliance improvement and user experience impact
        📖 View agent details and configuration →

        Common Pitfalls (And How to Avoid Them)

        "Let's Do Everything"

        Symptom: Trying 5 different AI tools simultaneously
        Result: Confusion, tool fatigue, no clear wins
        Fix: One tool, one team, one month

        "The Agent Will Fix It"

        Symptom: Deploying agents to broken processes
        Result: Faster failure
        Fix: Fix the process, then add agents

        "Trust Without Verification"

        Symptom: Accepting all agent suggestions blindly
        Result: Mysterious failures, team mistrust
        Fix: Every agent decision needs human review (initially)

        "Secret Experiments"

        Symptom: Not telling the team about agent usage
        Result: Shadow IT, duplicated effort
        Fix: Transparency from day one

        Measuring Success

        Track these metrics from day one:

        Efficiency Metrics

        Test creation time
        Bug discovery time
        Debugging time
        False positive rate

        Quality Metrics

        Bugs escaped to production
        Test coverage percentage
        Mean time to resolution
        Customer-reported issues

        Team Metrics (Most Important!)

        Developer satisfaction
        Adoption rate
        Tool usage frequency
        Knowledge sharing instances

        The Reality Check

        Here's what success actually looks like in the first 30 days:

        Realistic Wins

        • • 1-2 "aha!" moments
        • • 20-30% improvement in ONE area
        • • 3-5 team members interested
        • • 10+ lessons learned

        Unrealistic Expectations

        • • Complete transformation
        • • 10x improvements
        • • Full team adoption
        • • Zero failures

        Ready? Start Here:

        Prerequisites (Do This First):

        1.
        Install Claude Code: CLI or VS Code extension
        2.
        Ensure you have Node.js 18+ installed
        3.
        Install Agentic QE: npm install -g agentic-qe
        # Now, plan your first experiment:
        1. Open your terminal
        2. Create a new folder: agentic-qe-experiment
        3. Create a file: week1-baseline.md
        4. Write down:
        - Current biggest QE pain point
        - Time spent on it weekly
        - Impact when it fails
        - Dream outcome
        5. Commit it
        6. Share with one colleague
        print("Congratulations! You've started.")

        Final Thought

        The journey to Agentic QE isn't a sprint—it's not even a marathon. It's a continuous evolution. Start small, learn fast, fail safely, and scale what works.

        You don't need to see the whole staircase. Just take the first step.

        Welcome to the evolution.

        Questions? Stuck? Success story? Share in our community or reach out directly. We're all learning together.

          • Quality Criteria Recommender – HTSM v6.3 Quality Criteria analysis for shift-left quality engineering
          • Test Idea Rewriter – Transform passive test descriptions into active, observable test actions
          • QX Partner Agent – Quality Experience analysis combining QA advocacy and UX perspectives
          • Accessibility Auditor – WCAG 2.2 compliance testing with AI-powered remediation
          • 15 n8n Workflow Testing Agents – Complete testing suite for n8n automation including workflow execution, trigger testing, security auditing, chaos testing, CI/CD integration, and compliance validation

          • QCSD Refinement Swarm – BDD scenario generation and Gherkin feature file creation from requirements
          • QCSD Development Swarm – Implementation review with SHIP/CONDITIONAL/HOLD quality verdicts
          • QCSD CI/CD Swarm – Pipeline validation with RELEASE/REMEDIATE/BLOCK deployment verdicts

          QCSD Framework Integration

          Lalit's own Quality Engineering framework is now being integrated into the Agentic QE fleet, bringing structured methodologies for comprehensive quality assessment.

          Explore QCSD

          Foundational Inspirations

          Context-Driven School of Testing

          The philosophical foundation of adaptive quality practices

          The Context-Driven Testing approach fundamentally shaped how Agentic QE adapts to different project contexts. The principle that "best practices" depend on context directly influenced our Targeted (T) principle in PACT.

          "The value of any practice depends on its context."
          context-driven-testing.com

          Holistic Testing Model

          Lisa Crispin & Janet Gregory's whole-team approach to quality

          Lisa and Janet's Holistic Testing approach inspired our Collaborative (C) principle. Their vision of quality as a shared team responsibility directly translates to our human-agent collaboration model.

          "Quality is everyone's responsibility, built into every step."
          Holistic Testing for Agile Teams

          Software Testing Community

          Beyond the individuals named above, countless thought leaders in the software testing community have contributed ideas, challenged assumptions, and pushed the boundaries of what quality engineering can achieve.

          From exploratory testing pioneers to automation advocates, from risk-based testing practitioners to shift-left champions—your collective wisdom is woven into every aspect of this framework. A comprehensive list of acknowledgments is being compiled to properly honor these contributions.

          Join the Community

          The Agentic QE Framework is open source and welcomes contributions. Whether you're building new agents, creating skills, or sharing insights— your expertise can help shape the future of quality engineering.

                Symptom: Not telling the team about agent usage
                Result: Shadow IT, duplicated effort
                Fix: Transparency from day one

                Measuring Success

                Track these metrics from day one:

                Efficiency Metrics

                Test creation time
                Bug discovery time
                Debugging time
                False positive rate

                Quality Metrics

                Bugs escaped to production
                Test coverage percentage
                Mean time to resolution
                Customer-reported issues

                Team Metrics (Most Important!)

                Developer satisfaction
                Adoption rate
                Tool usage frequency
                Knowledge sharing instances

                The Reality Check

                Here's what success actually looks like in the first 30 days:

                Realistic Wins

                • • 1-2 "aha!" moments
                • • 20-30% improvement in ONE area
                • • 3-5 team members interested
                • • 10+ lessons learned

                Unrealistic Expectations

                • • Complete transformation
                • • 10x improvements
                • • Full team adoption
                • • Zero failures

                Ready? Start Here:

                Prerequisites (Do This First):

                1.
                Install Claude Code: CLI or VS Code extension
                2.
                Ensure you have Node.js 18+ installed
                3.
                Install Agentic QE: npm install -g agentic-qe
                # Now, plan your first experiment:
                1. Open your terminal
                2. Create a new folder: agentic-qe-experiment
                3. Create a file: week1-baseline.md
                4. Write down:
                - Current biggest QE pain point
                - Time spent on it weekly
                - Impact when it fails
                - Dream outcome
                5. Commit it
                6. Share with one colleague
                print("Congratulations! You've started.")

                Final Thought

                The journey to Agentic QE isn't a sprint—it's not even a marathon. It's a continuous evolution. Start small, learn fast, fail safely, and scale what works.

                You don't need to see the whole staircase. Just take the first step.

                Welcome to the evolution.

                Questions? Stuck? Success story? Share in our community or reach out directly. We're all learning together.

                  Agentic QE Assessment Guide

                  A comprehensive guide to assessing your organization's readiness and maturity for Agentic QE

                  Why Assessment Matters

                  "We need AI in our testing NOW!"

                  I hear this weekly. My response? "Show me your current testing first."

                  Because here's the truth: Agentic QE amplifies what exists. If you have chaos, you'll get faster chaos. If you have excellence, you'll get amplified excellence.

                  This assessment helps you understand:

                  • • Where you are today
                  • • What's possible tomorrow
                  • • What to fix first
                  • • Where agents will help most

                  The PACT Assessment Framework

                  # Each dimension is scored 0-100 based on current capabilities
                  class PACTAssessment:
                  def __init__(self):
                  self.dimensions = {
                  'Proactive': 0, # Anticipation capabilities
                  'Autonomous': 0, # Independence level
                  'Collaborative': 0, # Team integration
                  'Targeted': 0 # Focus and prioritization
                  }

                  Section 1: Proactive Capability Assessment
                  Score: 0/300

                  1.1 Failure Prediction - How does your team currently predict and prevent failures?

                  0 pts
                  We react when things break
                  25 pts
                  Basic monitoring alerts us to issues
                  50 pts
                  We analyze trends and patterns manually
                  75 pts
                  Some predictive analytics in place
                  100 pts
                  ML-based prediction with prevention

                  1.2 Risk Assessment - How do you identify risks in new features?

                  0 pts
                  We test and see what breaks
                  25 pts
                  Basic risk checklists
                  50 pts
                  Formal risk assessment sessions
                  75 pts
                  Data-driven risk scoring
                  100 pts
                  Automated risk analysis with historical data

                  1.3 Test Coverage Strategy - How do you decide what to test?

                  0 pts
                  Test everything we can think of
                  25 pts
                  Test critical paths only
                  50 pts
                  Risk-based test prioritization
                  75 pts
                  Dynamic coverage based on changes
                  100 pts
                  Predictive coverage optimization

                  Section 2: Autonomous Capability Assessment
                  Score: 0/300

                  2.1 Test Automation Level - What percentage of your tests are automated?

                  0 pts
                  < 10% automated
                  25 pts
                  10-30% automated
                  50 pts
                  30-50% automated
                  75 pts
                  50-70% automated
                  100 pts
                  > 70% automated

                  2.2 Self-Healing Capabilities - How do your tests handle changes?

                  0 pts
                  Manual updates for every change
                  25 pts
                  Some parameterization
                  50 pts
                  Smart locators and waits
                  75 pts
                  Self-healing selectors
                  100 pts
                  Autonomous test evolution

                  2.3 Deployment Automation - How automated is your deployment process?

                  0 pts
                  Fully manual deployment
                  25 pts
                  Scripted but manual trigger
                  50 pts
                  Automated with manual approval
                  75 pts
                  Fully automated to staging
                  100 pts
                  Automated with auto-rollback

                  Section 3: Collaborative Capability Assessment
                  Score: 0/300

                  3.1 Team Integration - How integrated is quality in your team?

                  0 pts
                  Separate QA team/phase
                  25 pts
                  QA involved in planning
                  50 pts
                  Developers write tests
                  75 pts
                  Whole team owns quality
                  100 pts
                  Quality-first culture

                  3.2 Knowledge Sharing - How is testing knowledge shared?

                  0 pts
                  No formal sharing
                  25 pts
                  Documentation exists
                  50 pts
                  Regular knowledge sessions
                  75 pts
                  Pairing and mentoring
                  100 pts
                  Continuous learning culture

                  3.3 Tool Integration - How integrated are your tools?

                  0 pts
                  Isolated tool silos
                  25 pts
                  Some manual integration
                  50 pts
                  Basic API integration
                  75 pts
                  Automated tool chain
                  100 pts
                  Seamless tool ecosystem

                  Section 4: Targeted Capability Assessment
                  Score: 0/300

                  4.1 Test Prioritization - How do you prioritize testing effort?

                  0 pts
                  Test everything equally
                  25 pts
                  Focus on new features
                  50 pts
                  Risk-based prioritization
                  75 pts
                  Data-driven prioritization
                  100 pts
                  Dynamic ML-based prioritization

                  4.2 Business Alignment - How aligned is testing with business goals?

                  0 pts
                  No clear connection
                  25 pts
                  Aware of business goals
                  50 pts
                  Tests map to user stories
                  75 pts
                  Tests map to business KPIs
                  100 pts
                  Direct business impact measurement

                  4.3 Value Measurement - How do you measure testing value?

                  0 pts
                  Count test cases
                  25 pts
                  Track bugs found
                  50 pts
                  Measure escaped defects
                  75 pts
                  Track business impact
                  100 pts
                  Continuous value optimization

                  Interpreting Your Results

                  0-240: Foundation Needed

                  Status: Focus on basics first
                  Agent Readiness: Not ready - would amplify chaos
                  Timeline: 3-6 months of foundation work
                  Priority Actions:
                  • Establish CI/CD pipeline
                  • Increase test automation
                  • Implement monitoring
                  • Build team collaboration

                  240-480: Ready for AI Assistance

                  Status: Can benefit from AI helpers
                  Agent Readiness: Ready for Level 1 agents
                  Timeline: 1-2 months to first value
                  Priority Actions:
                  • Introduce AI code completion
                  • Try AI-assisted test generation
                  • Implement anomaly detection
                  • Start with one team

                  480-720: Ready for Orchestration

                  Status: Multiple agents can work together
                  Agent Readiness: Ready for Level 2 systems
                  Timeline: 2-3 months to orchestration
                  Priority Actions:
                  • Deploy specialized agents
                  • Build orchestration layer
                  • Implement decision logging
                  • Expand to multiple teams

                  720-960: Ready for Autonomy

                  Status: Agents can self-direct
                  Agent Readiness: Ready for Level 3 autonomy
                  Timeline: 3-4 months to autonomy
                  Priority Actions:
                  • Enable autonomous operations
                  • Implement predictive systems
                  • Build trust through transparency
                  • Organization-wide rollout

                  960-1200: Ready for Partnership

                  Status: True human-agent collaboration
                  Agent Readiness: Ready for Level 4 partnership
                  Timeline: 6+ months to full partnership
                  Priority Actions:
                  • Agents as team members
                  • Bidirectional learning
                  • Strategic agent input
                  • Innovation partnership

                  Common Assessment Mistakes

                  Over-Optimistic Scoring

                  Symptom: All scores > 60
                  Reality Check: If you're that good, why do you need help?
                  Fix: Have team members assess independently, use lowest scores

                  Gaming the System

                  Symptom: Adjusting answers to justify tool purchase
                  Reality Check: Agents amplify reality, not wishes
                  Fix: Use objective metrics, not subjective feelings

                  Ignoring Weak Dimensions

                  Symptom: Focusing only on high scores
                  Reality Check: Weakest link determines system strength
                  Fix: Address lowest scores first

                  One-Time Assessment

                  Symptom: Assess once, never revisit
                  Reality Check: Maturity evolves continuously
                  Fix: Quarterly reassessment minimum

                  Your Assessment Action Plan

                  Step 1: Gather Your Team

                  • • Include developers, testers, ops
                  • • Book 2 hours
                  • • Prepare honestly

                  Step 2: Complete Assessment

                  • • Answer individually first
                  • • Discuss discrepancies
                  • • Agree on scores

                  Step 3: Identify Patterns

                  • • Find lowest dimension
                  • • Identify quick wins
                  • • Note dependencies

                  Step 4: Create 90-Day Plan

                  • • Week 1-2: Quick wins
                  • • Week 3-6: Foundation fixes
                  • • Week 7-12: First agent experiment

                  Step 5: Share Results

                  • • With leadership (for support)
                  • • With team (for buy-in)
                  • • With community (for guidance)

                  Need Help?

                  Assessment results surprising? Unsure about next steps?

                  Community Forum: Post in #assessment-help
                  Office Hours: Thursdays 2 PM UTC
                  1-on-1 Consultation: Book via calendar link
                  Email Support: assessment@agentic-qe.dev

                  Remember: The assessment isn't a judgment—it's a map. Now you know where you are and where you're going.

                      Agent Design Patterns

                      Proven patterns for designing effective QE agents that actually work in production

                      The Pattern Language of Agents

                      After evolving through 51 production-tested agents—featuring Queen-led orchestration and TDD specialists contributed by the community—these patterns emerged as the foundation for reliable QE automation. Each pattern has been refined through real-world deployments and continuous learning.

                      Think of these patterns like design patterns in software: reusable solutions to common problems.

                      The Scout

                      Explore unknown territories and report findings

                      Type:
                      Explorer
                      Autonomy:
                      High
                      Risk:
                      Low
                      Value:
                      Discovery

                      The Guardian

                      Protect production by monitoring and preventing issues

                      Type:
                      Protector
                      Autonomy:
                      Medium
                      Risk:
                      Medium
                      Value:
                      Prevention

                      The Validator

                      Ensure consistency and correctness across systems

                      Type:
                      Checker
                      Autonomy:
                      High
                      Risk:
                      Low
                      Value:
                      Consistency

                      The Synthesizer

                      Combine information from multiple sources to find insights

                      Type:
                      Analyzer
                      Autonomy:
                      Medium
                      Risk:
                      Low
                      Value:
                      Insight

                      The Healer

                      Automatically fix known issues without human intervention

                      Type:
                      Fixer
                      Autonomy:
                      Medium-High
                      Risk:
                      High
                      Value:
                      Availability

                      The Teacher

                      Learn from humans and teach other agents

                      Type:
                      Knowledge Manager
                      Autonomy:
                      Low-Medium
                      Risk:
                      Low
                      Value:
                      Learning

                      Composition Patterns

                      Agents work better together. Here are proven combinations:

                      The Investigation Squad

                      Scout
                      Finds the anomaly
                      Synthesizer
                      Correlates with other data
                      Validator
                      Confirms the issue
                      Teacher
                      Documents the finding

                      The Production Guard

                      Guardian
                      Watches for issues
                      Healer
                      Fixes known problems
                      Validator
                      Ensures fixes worked
                      Synthesizer
                      Learns from patterns

                      The Quality Ensemble

                      Scout
                      Explores new features
                      Validator
                      Checks correctness
                      Guardian
                      Monitors production
                      Teacher
                      Shares learnings

                      Anti-Patterns (What NOT to Do)

                      The Know-It-All
                      Problem: Agent tries to handle everything
                      Result: Jack of all trades, master of none
                      Fix: Specialized agents with clear boundaries
                      The Black Box
                      Problem: Agent can't explain decisions
                      Result: Zero trust from team
                      Fix: Explainability first, automation second
                      The Cowboy
                      Problem: Agent makes changes without oversight
                      Result: Unexpected production issues
                      Fix: Graduated autonomy with safeguards
                      The Chatterbox
                      Problem: Agent alerts on everything
                      Result: Alert fatigue, ignored warnings
                      Fix: Smart filtering and prioritization

                      Implementation Checklist

                      Before deploying any agent pattern:

                      Clear Purpose: One primary job
                      Defined Boundaries: What it can and cannot do
                      Explainable Actions: Every decision has a why
                      Graceful Failure: Knows when to ask for help
                      Learning Capability: Gets better over time
                      Human Override: Always possible
                      Audit Trail: Complete action history
                      Success Metrics: Measurable value

                      Success Metrics by Pattern

                      Track these metrics for each pattern:

                      Scout

                      Unknowns discovered per week

                      Guardian

                      Incidents prevented per month

                      Validator

                      Inconsistencies caught per day

                      Synthesizer

                      Actionable insights per week

                      Healer

                      MTTR improvement percentage

                      Teacher

                      Knowledge entries per sprint

                      Remember

                      Patterns are starting points, not rigid rules. Adapt them to your context. The best agent is the one that solves YOUR problem, not someone else's.

                      Real-World Agent Orchestration Patterns

                      Learn from production-tested orchestration patterns using actual QE agents. These patterns show how specialized agents coordinate to solve complex quality engineering challenges.

                      Pattern 1: Test Generation Pipeline

                      Event-Driven
                      qe-test-generator
                      →
                      qe-coverage-analyzer
                      →
                      qe-quality-gate

                      Goal: Generate comprehensive tests, analyze coverage gaps using O(log n) algorithms, and make intelligent go/no-go decisions.

                      COORDINATION CODE
                      // Event-driven coordination pattern
eventBus.on('tests:generated', async (event) => {
  // Test executor picks up generated tests
  await testExecutor.execute(event.tests);
});

eventBus.on('tests:completed', async (event) => {
  // Coverage analyzer processes results
  await coverageAnalyzer.analyze(event.results);
});

eventBus.on('coverage:analyzed', async (event) => {
  // Quality gate makes decision
  await qualityGate.decide(event.coverage);
});
                      View qe-test-generator →View qe-coverage-analyzer →View qe-quality-gate →
                      Key Benefit: 60% faster test generation with 92% edge case coverage. Agents coordinate via events without blocking, achieving 0.8ms message latency.

                      Pattern 2: Deployment Readiness Workflow

                      Parallel Execution
                      qe-security-scanner
                      →
                      qe-deployment-readiness
                      →
                      qe-regression-risk-analyzer

                      Goal: Scan for security vulnerabilities, assess overall deployment readiness, and intelligently select critical regression tests.

                      PARALLEL CONFIGURATION
                      // Multi-agent parallel execution
await fleet.orchestrate({
  strategy: 'parallel',
  agents: [
    {
      type: 'security-scanner',
      config: {
        scanTypes: ['SAST', 'DAST', 'dependency'],
        compliance: ['OWASP-Top-10', 'PCI-DSS']
      }
    },
    {
      type: 'deployment-readiness',
      config: {
        riskScoring: true,
        mlDecisions: true
      }
    },
    {
      type: 'regression-risk-analyzer',
      config: {
        smartSelection: true,
        coverageTarget: 0.95
      }
    }
  ]
});

                      Pattern 3: Production Intelligence Loop

                      Continuous Learning
                      qe-production-intelligence
                      →
                      qe-flaky-test-hunter
                      →
                      qe-test-generator
                      ↻

                      Goal: Learn from production incidents, hunt and stabilize flaky tests, generate new tests to prevent regression. The loop continues to improve quality.

                      CONTINUOUS LEARNING PATTERN
                      // Agent learning loop with shared memory
class LearningAgent extends BaseAgent {
  async learn(taskResult: TaskResult): Promise<void> {
    // Extract patterns from outcomes
    const patterns = this.analyzePatterns(taskResult);

    // Store in shared memory
    await this.memoryStore.store(
      `learnings/${this.id}`,
      patterns
    );

    // Update strategy
    this.strategy = this.adaptStrategy(patterns);

    // Share with fleet
    await this.eventBus.emit('learning:discovered', {
      agentId: this.id,
      patterns: patterns,
      confidence: this.calculateConfidence(patterns)
    });
  }
}

                      Self-Healing Results: Flaky test rate dropped from 8-12% to 0.3% (96% reduction). Agents improved by 23% over 3 months through continuous learning from production data.

                        Orchestration Strategies

                        How to coordinate multiple agents without creating chaos

                        The Orchestration Challenge

                        Picture this: 5 talented musicians, each playing perfectly. But no conductor. That's not music—it's noise.

                        I learned this the hard way when my 5 specialized agents nearly brought down production. Each was doing its job perfectly. Together? They were fighting over resources, duplicating work, and creating more problems than they solved.

                        Orchestration isn't optional. It's the difference between an agent mob and an agent team.

                        Core Orchestration Patterns

                        Pattern 1: Sequential Pipeline

                        Assembly Line

                        When to Use: Clear process flow, dependent steps

                        class SequentialOrchestrator:
    """
    Like an assembly line - each agent does its part in order.
    Simple, predictable, debuggable.
    """
    
    def orchestrate(self, task):
        pipeline = [
            ('scout', self.discover_test_scenarios),
            ('validator', self.validate_scenarios),
            ('executor', self.run_tests),
            ('synthesizer', self.analyze_results),
            ('reporter', self.generate_report)
        ]
        
        context = {'task': task, 'results': {}}
        
        for agent_name, agent_function in pipeline:
            try:
                result = agent_function(context)
                context['results'][agent_name] = result
                
                if result.status == 'critical_failure':
                    return self.handle_pipeline_failure(context, agent_name)
                    
            except Exception as e:
                return self.handle_agent_error(agent_name, e, context)
        
        return context['results']

                        Pros

                        • • Simple, predictable
                        • • Easy to debug
                        • • Clear dependencies

                        Cons

                        • • Slow (no parallelism)
                        • • Rigid workflow
                        • • Single point of failure

                        Pattern 2: Parallel Burst

                        Sprint Start

                        When to Use: Independent tasks, speed matters

                        class ParallelOrchestrator:
    """
    Like a sprint start - everyone runs at once.
    Fast but needs careful coordination.
    """
    
    def orchestrate(self, tasks):
        from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
        
        results = {}
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=10) as executor:
            # Launch all agents simultaneously
            future_to_agent = {
                executor.submit(agent.execute, task): agent 
                for agent, task in self.prepare_agent_tasks(tasks)
            }
            
            # Collect results as they complete
            for future in as_completed(future_to_agent):
                agent = future_to_agent[future]
                try:
                    result = future.result(timeout=30)
                    results[agent.name] = result
                except TimeoutError:
                    results[agent.name] = self.handle_timeout(agent)
                except Exception as e:
                    results[agent.name] = self.handle_error(agent, e)
        
        return self.merge_results(results)

                        Example: Our parallel burst pattern for API testing reduced a 5-minute test suite to 45 seconds by running 10 agents simultaneously on different endpoints.

                        Pattern 3: Event-Driven Choreography

                        Jazz Ensemble

                        When to Use: Complex workflows, reactive systems

                        class EventDrivenOrchestrator:
    """
    Like a jazz ensemble - everyone responds to what they hear.
    Flexible but requires clear communication.
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.event_bus = EventBus()
        self.agents = {}
        
    def register_agent(self, agent, subscribed_events):
        self.agents[agent.name] = agent
        for event_type in subscribed_events:
            self.event_bus.subscribe(event_type, agent.handle_event)
    
    def orchestrate(self):
        # Agents react to events, creating new events
        initial_event = Event('START_TESTING')
        self.event_bus.publish(initial_event)
        
        # Event chain example:
        # START_TESTING -> scout finds issue
        # ISSUE_FOUND -> validator confirms
        # ISSUE_CONFIRMED -> healer attempts fix
        # FIX_ATTEMPTED -> validator re-checks
        # VALIDATION_COMPLETE -> reporter summarizes

                        Pattern 4: Hierarchical Command

                        Military Operation

                        When to Use: Complex decisions, clear authority needed

                        class HierarchicalOrchestrator:
    """
    Like a military operation - clear chain of command.
    Efficient but can be rigid.
    """
    
    def orchestrate(self, mission):
        # Commander creates strategy
        strategy = self.commander.plan_mission(mission)
        
        # Distribute to squad leaders
        for objective in strategy.objectives:
            squad_leader = self.assign_squad_leader(objective)
            squad_leader.receive_orders(objective)
            
            # Squad leaders coordinate workers
            workers = self.assign_workers(objective)
            results = squad_leader.coordinate_workers(workers)
            
            # Report back up chain
            squad_leader.report_to_commander(results)
        
        return self.commander.mission_summary()

                        Pattern 5: Adaptive Mesh

                        Flock of Birds

                        When to Use: Dynamic environments, self-organizing teams

                        class AdaptiveMeshOrchestrator:
    """
    Like a flock of birds - no single leader, emergent coordination.
    Resilient but harder to predict.
    """
    
    def orchestrate(self):
        while not self.objective_complete():
            # Each agent decides independently based on shared state
            for agent in self.agents:
                agent_decision = agent.analyze_situation(self.shared_state)
                
                if agent_decision.should_act:
                    # Broadcast intention to prevent conflicts
                    agent.broadcast_intention(agent_decision)
                    
                    # Wait for objections
                    if not self.any_objections(agent_decision):
                        result = agent.execute(agent_decision)
                        self.shared_state.update(result)
                
            # Emergent behavior from simple rules
            self.adapt_to_results()

                        Orchestration Metrics

                        Efficiency

                        • • Agent utilization %
                        • • Average wait time
                        • • Tasks per hour

                        Reliability

                        • • Failure rate per day
                        • • Mean recovery time
                        • • Deadlock frequency

                        Coordination

                        • • Message latency
                        • • Conflict rate
                        • • Resource contention

                        Common Orchestration Failures

                        The Thundering Herd

                        All agents start simultaneously, overwhelming resources

                        Solution: Staged startup with resource pre-allocation

                        The Deadly Embrace

                        Agent A waits for B, B waits for A

                        Solution: Timeout + deadlock detection

                        The Broken Telephone

                        Message corruption/loss between agents

                        Solution: Message acknowledgment + retry logic

                        The Leader Election Crisis

                        Multiple agents think they're in charge

                        Solution: Clear hierarchy or consensus protocol

                        The Golden Rules

                        1

                        Start Sequential: You can always parallelize later

                        2

                        Monitor Everything: You can't optimize what you don't measure

                        3

                        Plan for Failure: Agents will fail, orchestration must survive

                        4

                        Human Override: Always have a kill switch

                        5

                        Clear Communication: Agents must speak the same language

                        Advanced: Self-Learning Orchestration

                        The AQE fleet now includes self-learning capabilities with 4 reinforcement learning algorithms and a multi-model router that achieves 70-81% cost savings while maintaining quality.

                        Self-Learning System

                        • 4 RL Algorithms: Q-Learning, SARSA, Actor-Critic, Decision Transformer
                        • 85%+ Pattern Reuse: Agents learn from past decisions
                        • Continuous Improvement: 23% better performance over 3 months

                        Multi-Model Router

                        • 300+ Models: Intelligent model selection per task
                        • 70-81% Cost Savings: Right-size model for each operation
                        • Code Intelligence: 80% token reduction via semantic search
                        SELF-LEARNING ORCHESTRATION
                        // Agents that learn and improve autonomously
class LearningOrchestrator:
    def __init__(self):
        self.pattern_memory = PatternMemory()  # 85%+ reuse
        self.model_router = MultiModelRouter()  # 70-81% savings

    def orchestrate(self, task):
        # Check for learned patterns
        cached_strategy = self.pattern_memory.find_similar(task)
        if cached_strategy and cached_strategy.confidence > 0.9:
            return self.execute_cached(cached_strategy)

        # Select optimal model for task complexity
        model = self.model_router.select(task.complexity)

        # Execute with learning enabled
        result = self.execute_with_learning(task, model)

        # Store patterns for future reuse
        self.pattern_memory.store(task, result)
        return result

                          Human-in-the-Loop Workflows

                          Because the best agentic systems augment humans, not replace them

                          The Trust Equation

                          Here's the uncomfortable truth: Your agents will be wrong. Sometimes catastrophically.

                          A payment validation agent once approved a $0.01 transaction for a $10,000 order. Technically, the payment went through. The agent was "correct." The business logic? Not so much.

                          That's why human-in-the-loop isn't a limitation—it's a feature.

                          The Spectrum of Human Involvement

                          Level 0: Full ManualHuman does everything
                          Level 1: Agent SuggestsHuman decides and acts
                          Level 2: Agent Acts with ApprovalHuman approves, agent acts
                          Level 3: Agent Acts, Human AuditsAgent acts, human reviews
                          Level 4: Agent Acts, Alerts on Edge CasesHuman handles exceptions
                          Level 5: Full AutonomousHuman sets policy only

                          Most successful implementations operate at Level 2-4. Here's why and how.

                          Human-in-the-Loop Patterns

                          Pattern 1: The Approval Gate

                          Agent Proposes, Human Disposes

                          When to Use: High-risk actions, learning phase, compliance requirements

                          class ApprovalGateWorkflow:
    """
    Agent proposes, human disposes.
    Safe, controlled, builds trust gradually.
    """
    
    def agent_action_flow(self, agent, action):
        # Agent analyzes and prepares action
        proposal = agent.prepare_action(action)
        
        # Add context for human decision
        proposal_package = {
            'action': proposal,
            'confidence': agent.calculate_confidence(proposal),
            'impact': agent.assess_impact(proposal),
            'reasoning': agent.explain_reasoning(proposal),
            'alternatives': agent.suggest_alternatives(proposal),
            'risks': agent.identify_risks(proposal)
        }
        
        # Request human approval
        decision = self.wait_for_human(proposal_package)
        
        if decision.approved:
            result = agent.execute_action(proposal)
        
        # Learn from human decision
        agent.learn_from_decision(proposal, decision)

                          Example: Our deployment agent has 94% approval rate after 6 months. The 6% rejections? All would have caused issues. Human judgment still matters.

                          Pattern 2: The Escalation Ladder

                          Graduated Response

                          When to Use: Graduated response system, 24/7 operations

                          High Confidence

                          Auto-handle
                          Notify with auto

                          Medium Confidence

                          Request guidance
                          Require approval

                          Low Confidence

                          Immediate escalation

                          Pattern 3: The Shadow Mode

                          Learning Phase

                          When to Use: Building trust, training agents, validating changes

                          class ShadowModeWorkflow:
    """
    Agent shadows human decisions to learn.
    Safe way to validate agent readiness.
    """
    
    def shadow_operation(self):
        while self.in_shadow_mode():
            # Human makes decision
            human_decision = self.capture_human_decision()
            
            # Agent makes same decision independently
            agent_decision = self.agent.make_decision(
                same_context=human_decision.context
            )
            
            # Compare decisions
            agreement = self.compare_decisions(
                human_decision, agent_decision
            )
            
            # Learn from disagreements
            if not agreement.matches:
                self.agent.learn_from_disagreement(
                    human_decision, agent_decision
                )
                          Week 1
                          62% agreement
                          Learning
                          Week 2
                          78% agreement
                          Improving
                          Week 3
                          91% agreement
                          Ready!

                          Pattern 4: The Review Loop

                          Quality Assurance

                          When to Use: Continuous improvement, quality assurance

                          class ReviewLoopWorkflow:
    """
    Agent acts, human reviews sample.
    Balances speed with quality control.
    """
    
    def agent_action_with_review(self, action):
        # Agent executes action
        result = self.agent.execute(action)
        
        # Determine if review needed (e.g., 10% sample)
        if self.should_review(action, result):
            self.queue_for_review(action, result)
        
        return result
    
    def human_review_process(self):
        # Daily/weekly review sessions
        for item in self.review_queue:
            review_result = self.human_review(item)
            
            if review_result.incorrect:
                # Train agent on mistake
                self.agent.learn_from_error(item, review_result)

                          Pattern 5: The Teaching Loop

                          Interactive Learning

                          When to Use: Complex domains, continuous learning

                          Present Scenario
                          Human shows problem
                          Agent Attempts
                          AI tries solution
                          Human Teaches
                          Shows correct way
                          Agent Learns
                          Applies knowledge

                          Trust Building Timeline

                          Week 1-2
                          Shadow Mode
                          100% human effort
                          Week 3-4
                          Suggestion
                          90% human effort
                          Week 5-8
                          Supervised
                          60% human effort
                          Week 9-12
                          Delegated
                          30% human effort
                          Month 4+
                          Partnership
                          10% human effort

                          The Golden Rules of Human-in-the-Loop

                          1

                          Humans Have Veto Power: Always, no exceptions

                          2

                          Context Is Everything: Never escalate without full context

                          3

                          Learn from Every Interaction: Each decision is a teaching moment

                          4

                          Respect Cognitive Load: Don't overwhelm with decisions

                          5

                          Build Trust Gradually: Earn autonomy through competence

                          6

                          Make Handoffs Smooth: Seamless human-agent transition

                          7

                          Explain Everything: Humans need to understand to trust

                          Common Pitfalls

                          Alert Fatigue

                          Too many escalations

                          Solution: Better filtering, priority queues

                          Context Loss

                          Human doesn't understand situation

                          Solution: Rich handoff packages

                          Trust Erosion

                          Agent makes bad decision

                          Solution: Transparent post-mortems

                          Skill Atrophy

                          Humans forget how to do tasks

                          Solution: Regular manual sessions

                          The Bottom Line

                          Human-in-the-loop isn't about limitation—it's about leverage. The best agentic systems make humans more effective, not obsolete. They handle the routine so humans can focus on the exceptional.

                          Start with humans doing 90%, agents 10%. Evolve based on demonstrated competence. The goal isn't to eliminate humans—it's to eliminate tedium.

                              Domain-Driven Quality Engineering

                              Organize agents by capability domain for scalable, maintainable QE fleets

                              V3 Feature

                              Why Domain-Driven Organization?

                              In V3, agents are organized into capability domains rather than flat lists. This enables better scaling, clearer responsibility boundaries, and intelligent cross-domain workflows.

                              Think of domains like departments in a company: each has its specialty, but they collaborate on shared goals.

                              Available Domains

                              core

                              3 agents

                              Essential QE functions available to all projects

                              qe-test-generatorqe-coverage-analyzerqe-test-executor

                              security

                              3 agents

                              Security scanning, vulnerability detection, compliance

                              qe-security-scannerqe-vulnerability-analyzerqe-compliance-checker

                              performance

                              3 agents

                              Load testing, profiling, optimization recommendations

                              qe-performance-testerqe-profilerqe-bottleneck-analyzer

                              accessibility

                              3 agents

                              WCAG compliance, screen reader testing, inclusive design

                              a11y-allyqx-partnerwcag-validator

                              chaos

                              3 agents

                              Resilience testing, fault injection, disaster recovery

                              qe-chaos-engineerqe-resilience-testerqe-failover-validator

                              browser

                              3 agents

                              E2E testing, visual regression, cross-browser validation

                              browser-automation-agentvisual-regression-testercross-browser-validator

                              Domain Selection by Team Size

                              1-3 developers

                              Topology: mesh
                              Max 5 agents
                              Recommended: core
                              Optional: security

                              4-8 developers

                              Topology: hierarchical
                              Max 8 agents
                              Recommended: core, security
                              Optional: performance, accessibility

                              9-15 developers

                              Topology: hierarchical-mesh
                              Max 15 agents
                              Recommended: core, security, performance
                              Optional: accessibility, chaos, browser

                              15+ developers

                              Topology: hierarchical-mesh
                              Max 25 agents
                              Recommended: core, security, performance, chaos
                              Optional: accessibility, browser, custom

                              Cross-Domain Workflow Patterns

                              Pattern: Security-First Development

                              core
                              security
                              core
                              # Security-first workflow: scan before test
aqe workflow create --name security-first \
  --steps "security:scan -> core:generate-tests -> core:execute"

# Agents coordinate automatically via claims system

                              Pattern: Full-Stack Quality Gate

                              core
                              security
                              performance
                              accessibility
                              # Parallel quality gate across all domains
aqe workflow create --name full-stack-gate \
  --parallel "core,security,performance,accessibility" \
  --gate "all-pass" \
  --timeout 300

                              Pattern: Chaos-Resilience Validation

                              core
                              chaos
                              core
                              # Test normal -> inject fault -> verify recovery
aqe workflow create --name chaos-validation \
  --steps "core:baseline -> chaos:inject -> core:verify-recovery" \
  --rollback-on-failure

                              Fleet Configuration Example

                              # Initialize fleet with specific domains
npx @claude-flow/cli@latest swarm init \
  --topology hierarchical \
  --max-agents 10 \
  --domains core,security,performance

# Or via configuration file (.aqe/config.yaml)
fleet:
  topology: hierarchical
  maxAgents: 10
  domains:
    - name: core
      enabled: true
      priority: 1
    - name: security
      enabled: true
      priority: 2
    - name: performance
      enabled: true
      priority: 3

  # Domain-specific settings
  domainConfig:
    security:
      scanOnCommit: true
      blockOnCritical: true
    performance:
      thresholds:
        responseTime: 200ms
        memoryLimit: 512MB

                              Best Practices

                              Do

                              • Start with core domain only
                              • Add domains incrementally based on needs
                              • Use cross-domain workflows for complex tasks
                              • Monitor domain-level metrics

                              Avoid

                              • Enabling all domains at once
                              • Mixing domain responsibilities
                              • Ignoring domain priority settings
                              • Creating circular domain dependencies

                                Intelligent Model Routing

                                TinyDancer 3-tier system: Right model for the right task, every time

                                V3 Feature - ADR-026

                                Why Model Routing Matters

                                70-81%
                                Cost Reduction
                                3x
                                Faster Simple Tasks
                                Same
                                Quality for Complex Tasks

                                The 3-Tier System

                                Tier 1: Agent Booster

                                Local / Cached
                                <1ms$0
                                Best for:
                                • Simple transforms (var -> const)
                                • Add type annotations
                                • Remove console.log statements
                                • Format code

                                Tier 2: Haiku

                                claude-3-haiku
                                ~500ms$0.0002/task
                                Best for:
                                • Simple bug fixes (1-2 lines)
                                • Basic test generation
                                • Documentation updates
                                • Low complexity refactoring

                                Tier 3: Sonnet/Opus

                                claude-3.5-sonnet / claude-3-opus
                                2-5s$0.003-$0.015/task
                                Best for:
                                • Architecture decisions
                                • Security audits
                                • Complex reasoning
                                • Multi-file refactoring

                                Complexity Scoring (0-100)

                                Tasks are automatically scored based on these factors to determine the optimal model tier:

                                15%
                                Lines changed
                                0-10 lines = low, 10-50 = medium, 50+ = high
                                20%
                                Files affected
                                1 file = low, 2-5 = medium, 5+ = high
                                25%
                                Domain complexity
                                Security/architecture = high, formatting = low
                                20%
                                Context required
                                How much codebase knowledge needed
                                20%
                                Risk level
                                Production impact potential

                                Scoring Thresholds

                                0-25: Tier 1 (Agent Booster)
                                26-60: Tier 2 (Haiku)
                                61-100: Tier 3 (Sonnet/Opus)

                                Real-World Examples

                                TaskScoreTierCostReason
                                Fix typo in error message
                                5
                                		Haiku$0.0005Single line change, no context needed
                                Generate unit tests for UserService
                                45
                                		Sonnet$0.003Requires understanding class structure and dependencies
                                Security audit for auth module
                                85
                                		Opus$0.045High risk, requires deep security expertise
                                Add missing TypeScript types
                                15
                                		Haiku$0.0008Pattern-based, low context requirement
                                Refactor monolith to microservices
                                95
                                		Opus$0.05+Architecture decision, high complexity

                                Cost Optimization Strategies

                                Automatic Optimizations

                                • Pattern caching: Reuse successful patterns (85%+ reuse rate)
                                • Batch processing: Group similar tasks for efficiency
                                • Token reduction: 80% fewer tokens via semantic search
                                • Smart fallback: Start with Haiku, escalate only if needed

                                Configuration Options

                                # .aqe/config.yaml
modelRouting:
  preferCost: true  # Favor cheaper models
  maxTier: 2        # Cap at Haiku for cost control

  # Override for specific domains
  overrides:
    security:
      minTier: 3    # Always use Opus for security
    formatting:
      maxTier: 1    # Only Agent Booster for formatting

                                CLI Usage

                                # Get routing recommendation before task
                                npx @claude-flow/cli@latest hooks pre-task --description "Fix typo in README"
                                Output: Tier 1 (Agent Booster) - Estimated cost: $0
                                # Record outcome for learning
                                npx @claude-flow/cli@latest hooks model-outcome --task "Fix typo" --model haiku --outcome success
                                # View routing statistics
                                npx @claude-flow/cli@latest hooks model-stats

                                When to Override Automatic Routing

                                Force Higher Tier When:

                                • - Security-critical operations
                                • - Customer-facing features
                                • - Compliance requirements
                                • - Novel/unprecedented tasks

                                Force Lower Tier When:

                                • - Budget constraints
                                • - High-volume repetitive tasks
                                • - Development/testing environments
                                • - Well-understood patterns
