                                  Queen Coordinator Orchestration

                                  Hierarchical coordination with intelligent task distribution and consensus

                                  V3 Feature

                                  The Queen Coordinator Pattern

                                  The Queen Coordinator is a specialized agent that orchestrates the entire fleet. Unlike flat mesh topologies where agents coordinate peer-to-peer, the Queen provides:

                                  Intelligent Dispatch

                                  Routes tasks to optimal workers based on load, expertise, and availability

                                  Consensus Management

                                  Coordinates voting for critical decisions requiring agreement

                                  Work Stealing

                                  Automatically rebalances work from overloaded or stuck agents

                                  Task Submission Patterns

                                  Direct Assignment

                                  Queen assigns task to specific worker

                                  Use case: Known expertise match
                                  aqe task submit --task "Generate tests" --assign worker-1

                                  Pool Submission

                                  Queen adds task to pool, workers claim

                                  Use case: Load balancing, flexible assignment
                                  aqe task submit --task "Analyze coverage" --pool general

                                  Broadcast

                                  All workers receive and collaborate

                                  Use case: Large tasks requiring multiple agents
                                  aqe task submit --task "Security audit" --broadcast --require-consensus

                                  Work-Stealing Configuration

                                  Work stealing allows idle agents to take tasks from overloaded agents, ensuring optimal utilization across the fleet.

                                  Stealing Triggers

                                  • Stale threshold: Task untouched for N minutes
                                  • Load imbalance: Worker has 3x average load
                                  • Explicit mark: Worker marks task as stealable
                                  • Health check: Worker becomes unresponsive

                                  Configuration

                                  # .aqe/config.yaml
workStealing:
  enabled: true
  staleThresholdMinutes: 15
  loadImbalanceRatio: 3.0
  preferSameType: true  # Prefer matching agent types

  # Protect certain tasks from stealing
  protected:
    - security-audit
    - compliance-check

                                  Claims System

                                  The claims system tracks who is working on what, preventing duplicate work and enabling smooth handoffs.

                                  available
                                  No one working on issue
                                  claimed
                                  Agent actively working
                                  paused
                                  Work temporarily stopped
                                  blocked
                                  Waiting on external dependency
                                  stealable
                                  Can be taken by another agent
                                  completed
                                  Work finished successfully

                                  Claims CLI Commands

                                  # Claim an issue
                                  aqe claims claim --issue 123 --agent worker-1
                                  # Release a claim
                                  aqe claims release --issue 123
                                  # Handoff to another agent
                                  aqe claims handoff --issue 123 --to worker-2
                                  # View claims board
                                  aqe claims board

                                  Consensus Voting Workflows

                                  For critical decisions, the Queen can initiate consensus voting among workers.

                                  Voting Process

                                  1. Queen Proposes
                                  2. Workers Analyze
                                  3. Cast Votes
                                  4. Consensus/Fail
                                  # Propose a change requiring consensus
aqe consensus propose \
  --type "architecture" \
  --description "Switch from REST to GraphQL" \
  --threshold 0.75 \
  --timeout 300

# Workers vote
aqe consensus vote --proposal-id abc123 --vote approve --reason "Better type safety"

# Check status
aqe consensus status --proposal-id abc123

                                  Consensus Algorithms

                                  • simple-majority
                                    >50% agreement
                                  • supermajority
                                    >75% agreement
                                  • unanimous
                                    100% agreement
                                  • weighted
                                    Expertise-weighted votes

                                  Use Consensus For

                                  • Architecture decisions
                                  • Security policy changes
                                  • Breaking API changes
                                  • Deployment go/no-go

                                  Example: Complete Workflow Orchestration

                                  #!/bin/bash
# Example: Feature Development Workflow with Queen Coordination

# 1. Initialize fleet with Queen
npx @claude-flow/cli@latest swarm init --topology hierarchical --queen-enabled

# 2. Spawn workers
aqe hive-mind spawn --count 5 --role worker

# 3. Submit feature task to Queen
aqe task submit \
  --type feature \
  --description "Add user authentication with OAuth" \
  --priority high

# Queen automatically:
# - Analyzes task complexity (Score: 75 -> Tier 3)
# - Breaks into subtasks (design, implement, test, review)
# - Assigns to available workers based on expertise
# - Monitors progress and rebalances if needed

# 4. Monitor progress
aqe claims board

# Output:
# +-----------+----------+--------+----------+
# | Issue     | Agent    | Status | Progress |
# +-----------+----------+--------+----------+
# | auth-1    | worker-1 | active | 45%      |
# | auth-2    | worker-2 | active | 30%      |
# | auth-3    | worker-3 | paused | 0%       |
# +-----------+----------+--------+----------+

# 5. Worker-3 is stuck, mark as stealable
aqe claims mark-stealable --issue auth-3 --reason blocked-timeout

# 6. Worker-4 steals the task
aqe claims steal --issue auth-3 --stealer worker-4

# 7. All tasks complete, request consensus for merge
aqe consensus propose \
  --type deployment \
  --description "Merge auth feature to main" \
  --threshold 0.75

# 8. Workers vote based on their testing results
# Consensus reached -> Queen approves merge

                                  Anti-Patterns to Avoid

                                  Queen Bottleneck

                                  All tasks routed through Queen, causing delays

                                  Fix: Enable direct worker-to-worker for simple handoffs

                                  Consensus Paralysis

                                  Requiring consensus for trivial decisions

                                  Fix: Only use consensus for high-impact decisions

                                  Aggressive Stealing

                                  Tasks stolen before workers finish context loading

                                  Fix: Increase stale threshold, add grace period

                                  Claim Hoarding

                                  Agents claiming more tasks than they can handle

                                  Fix: Set maxClaims per agent, enable auto-release

                                    Learning & Self-Improvement

                                    ReasoningBank integration, dream cycles, and pattern transfer

                                    V3 Feature - SONA System

                                    Self-Organizing Neural Architecture (SONA)

                                    V3 agents don't just execute - they learn and improve. The SONA system enables continuous learning from task outcomes, building a ReasoningBank of patterns that improve over time.

                                    85%+
                                    Pattern Reuse Rate
                                    23%
                                    Performance Improvement (3 months)
                                    150x
                                    Faster Pattern Search (HNSW)

                                    ReasoningBank Integration

                                    ReasoningBank is a vector database optimized for storing and retrieving reasoning patterns. Agents store successful strategies and retrieve similar patterns for new tasks.

                                    Storage Structure

                                    // Pattern stored in ReasoningBank
{
  id: "pattern-uuid",
  embedding: [0.12, 0.45, ...],  // 384-dim
  metadata: {
    task_type: "test-generation",
    domain: "core",
    confidence: 0.92,
    success_rate: 0.89,
    usage_count: 147
  },
  reasoning: {
    context: "React component with hooks",
    strategy: "Mock dependencies, test hooks lifecycle",
    outcome: "Generated 15 tests, 94% coverage"
  }
}

                                    CLI Commands

                                    # Store a pattern
                                    aqe intelligence pattern-store --pattern "..." --type test-gen
                                    # Search similar patterns
                                    aqe intelligence pattern-search --query "React hooks testing"
                                    # View statistics
                                    aqe intelligence stats --detailed

                                    Reinforcement Learning Algorithms

                                    SONA supports 4 RL algorithms, automatically selecting the best one based on task characteristics:

                                    Q-Learning

                                    Value-based learning for discrete action spaces

                                    Use: Task routing decisions
                                    Simple, proven

                                    SARSA

                                    On-policy learning with safer exploration

                                    Use: Risk-sensitive operations
                                    Conservative updates

                                    Actor-Critic

                                    Combines value and policy learning

                                    Use: Complex multi-step tasks
                                    Stable convergence

                                    Decision Transformer

                                    Sequence modeling for decision making

                                    Use: Long-horizon planning
                                    Context-aware

                                    Trajectory Recording

                                    # Start trajectory for a task
aqe intelligence trajectory-start --task "Generate API tests"

# Record steps
aqe intelligence trajectory-step \
  --action "analyze-openapi-spec" \
  --result "Found 15 endpoints" \
  --quality 0.9

# End trajectory with outcome
aqe intelligence trajectory-end --success true --feedback "Tests passed"

                                    Dream Cycle Scheduling

                                    Like biological sleep consolidates memories, dream cycles consolidate learned patterns during idle periods. This prevents catastrophic forgetting and promotes pattern generalization.

                                    1

                                    Collect

                                    Gather trajectories from recent tasks

                                    Continuous
                                    2

                                    Replay

                                    Revisit and analyze successful patterns

                                    ~5 min
                                    3

                                    Consolidate

                                    EWC++ memory consolidation

                                    ~10 min
                                    4

                                    Prune

                                    Remove low-value patterns

                                    ~2 min
                                    5

                                    Promote

                                    Elevate high-confidence patterns to global

                                    ~1 min

                                    Schedule Configuration

                                    # .aqe/config.yaml
learning:
  dreamCycle:
    enabled: true
    schedule: "0 2 * * *"  # Run at 2 AM daily
    minIdleMinutes: 30      # Or when idle for 30 min

    # EWC++ consolidation settings
    consolidation:
      importanceThreshold: 0.7
      retentionRate: 0.95
      maxPatterns: 10000

                                    Pattern Promotion Workflow

                                    Patterns progress through confidence levels before becoming globally available:

                                    Local (0-0.5)
                                    Tentative (0.5-0.7)
                                    Confirmed (0.7-0.9)
                                    Global (0.9+)

                                    Promotion Criteria

                                    • Success rate > 80% over 10+ uses
                                    • Consistency across different contexts
                                    • No negative feedback from humans
                                    • Passes cross-validation on held-out tasks

                                    Manual Override

                                    # Force promote a pattern
aqe intelligence pattern-promote \
  --pattern-id abc123 \
  --level global \
  --reason "Validated by team"

# Demote a bad pattern
aqe intelligence pattern-demote \
  --pattern-id def456 \
  --reason "Caused test failures"

                                    Cross-Project Transfer

                                    Transfer learned patterns from one project to another, accelerating learning on new codebases:

                                    Transfer Command

                                    # Transfer patterns from source project
npx @claude-flow/cli@latest hooks transfer \
  --sourcePath /path/to/mature-project \
  --minConfidence 0.8 \
  --filter "test-generation,security"

# Output:
# Transferred 147 patterns from source project
# - test-generation: 89 patterns
# - security: 58 patterns
# Filtered out 23 patterns below confidence threshold

                                    Transfer Recommendations

                                    • Transfer from similar tech stacks
                                    • Start with high-confidence patterns only
                                    • Monitor pattern performance post-transfer
                                    • Allow adaptation period before evaluation

                                    Avoid Transferring

                                    • Project-specific patterns (custom frameworks)
                                    • Low-confidence or experimental patterns
                                    • Patterns from very different domains
                                    • Outdated patterns (older than 6 months)

                                      Browser Automation Playbook

                                      E2E testing, accessibility validation, and visual regression with Vibium

                                      V3 Feature

                                      Vibium vs Agent-Browser Comparison

                                      V3 supports two browser automation approaches. Choose based on your needs:

                                      FeatureVibiumAgent-BrowserRecommended
                                      AI-Powered ActionsNatural language commandsRef-based (@e1, @e2)
                                      vibium
                                      SpeedModerate (AI processing)Fast (direct refs)
                                      agent-browser
                                      Accessibility TestingReal axe-core + AI analysisBasic snapshot
                                      vibium
                                      Visual RegressionBuilt-in with AI diffManual setup required
                                      vibium
                                      Learning CostLow (natural language)Medium (ref system)
                                      vibium
                                      DeterminismLower (AI variance)High (explicit refs)
                                      agent-browser

                                      Use Vibium When:

                                      • - Accessibility testing is critical
                                      • - Natural language test authoring preferred
                                      • - Visual regression needed
                                      • - Non-technical stakeholders write tests

                                      Use Agent-Browser When:

                                      • - Speed is paramount
                                      • - Deterministic tests required
                                      • - Complex DOM interactions
                                      • - CI/CD performance matters

                                      Real axe-core Accessibility Testing

                                      Vibium integrates real axe-core (not simulated) for WCAG 2.2 compliance testing. Results are analyzed by AI for actionable remediation advice.

                                      Common Rules Checked

                                      serious
                                      color-contrast

                                      Text contrast ratio requirements

                                      critical
                                      label

                                      Form inputs must have labels

                                      critical
                                      image-alt

                                      Images must have alt text

                                      serious
                                      keyboard

                                      All functionality via keyboard

                                      moderate
                                      aria-roles

                                      ARIA roles must be valid

                                      moderate
                                      heading-order

                                      Headings in logical order

                                      Testing Command

                                      # Run accessibility audit on a page
aqe a11y audit --url https://example.com \
  --wcag-level AA \
  --output report.html

# Example output:
# Accessibility Audit Results
# ==========================
# Total Issues: 12
# - Critical: 2
# - Serious: 5
# - Moderate: 5
#
# Top Issues:
# 1. [critical] img missing alt text (3 instances)
# 2. [critical] form input without label (1 instance)
# 3. [serious] color contrast 3.5:1 (min 4.5:1)

                                      CI Integration

                                      # .github/workflows/a11y.yml
- name: Accessibility Check
  run: |
    aqe a11y audit --url ${{ secrets.STAGING_URL }} \
      --wcag-level AA \
      --fail-on critical,serious \
      --output a11y-report.html

- name: Upload Report
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
  with:
    name: accessibility-report
    path: a11y-report.html

                                      Visual Regression Setup

                                      Catch unintended visual changes with AI-powered screenshot comparison. Vibium understands layout intent, reducing false positives from minor pixel shifts.

                                      Initialize Visual Baseline

                                      # Create baseline screenshots
aqe visual init --url https://example.com \
  --pages "/" "/about" "/contact" \
  --viewports "mobile,tablet,desktop" \
  --baseline-dir ./visual-baselines

# Output:
# Created 9 baseline screenshots
# - home-mobile.png
# - home-tablet.png
# - home-desktop.png
# ... (6 more)

                                      Run Visual Comparison

                                      # Compare against baseline
aqe visual compare --url https://staging.example.com \
  --baseline-dir ./visual-baselines \
  --threshold 0.02 \
  --ai-analysis

# Output:
# Visual Regression Results
# =========================
# Pages Checked: 9
# Passed: 7
# Failed: 2
#
# Failures:
# 1. home-desktop.png
#    - Diff: 3.4% (threshold: 2%)
#    - AI Analysis: "Button color changed from #007bff to #0056b3"
#    - Recommendation: Intentional? Update baseline.
#
# 2. about-mobile.png
#    - Diff: 12.1%
#    - AI Analysis: "Navigation menu overlapping content"
#    - Recommendation: Bug - investigate CSS changes

                                      Best Practices

                                      • Use consistent viewport sizes
                                      • Hide dynamic content (timestamps, ads)
                                      • Wait for animations to complete
                                      • Version baselines with code

                                      Common Pitfalls

                                      • Too low threshold = false positives
                                      • Too high threshold = missed bugs
                                      • Font rendering varies by OS
                                      • Retina vs non-retina displays

                                      E2E Test Generation

                                      Generate Playwright/Cypress tests from user journey descriptions using AI:

                                      Input: Natural Language

                                      # User journey description
aqe e2e generate --journey "
  1. User visits homepage
  2. Clicks 'Sign Up' button
  3. Fills in email, password, confirm password
  4. Clicks 'Create Account'
  5. Sees welcome message with their email
  6. Can access dashboard
" --framework playwright

                                      Output: Playwright Test

                                      import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('user signup flow', async ({ page }) => {
  // 1. Visit homepage
  await page.goto('/');

  // 2. Click Sign Up
  await page.click('text=Sign Up');

  // 3. Fill form
  await page.fill('[name="email"]', 'test@example.com');
  await page.fill('[name="password"]', 'SecurePass123!');
  await page.fill('[name="confirmPassword"]', 'SecurePass123!');

  // 4. Submit
  await page.click('button:has-text("Create Account")');

  // 5. Verify welcome
  await expect(page.locator('.welcome-message'))
    .toContainText('test@example.com');

  // 6. Verify dashboard access
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/dashboard/);
});

                                        Fleet Configuration Playbook

                                        Topology selection, anti-drift configuration, and scaling strategies

                                        V3 Configuration

                                        Topology Selection by Team Size

                                        mesh

                                        1-3 developers
                                        Max 5 agents

                                        Peer-to-peer, all agents equal

                                        Pros

                                        • - Simple setup
                                        • - Low overhead
                                        • - Direct communication

                                        Cons

                                        • - Limited scaling
                                        • - No central coordination
                                        Best for: Small projects, individual developers
                                        npx @claude-flow/cli@latest swarm init \
  --topology mesh \
  --max-agents 5 \
  --strategy specialized

                                        hierarchical

                                        4-8 developers
                                        Max 10 agents

                                        Queen coordinator with worker tiers

                                        Pros

                                        • - Clear authority
                                        • - Better scaling
                                        • - Work stealing

                                        Cons

                                        • - Queen bottleneck possible
                                        • - More configuration
                                        Best for: Small teams, moderate complexity
                                        npx @claude-flow/cli@latest swarm init \
  --topology hierarchical \
  --max-agents 10 \
  --strategy specialized

                                        hierarchical-mesh

                                        9-15+ developers
                                        Max 25 agents

                                        Hybrid with domain-specific sub-meshes

                                        Pros

                                        • - Best of both
                                        • - Domain isolation
                                        • - High resilience

                                        Cons

                                        • - Complex setup
                                        • - Higher resource usage
                                        Best for: Large teams, enterprise projects
                                        npx @claude-flow/cli@latest swarm init \
  --topology hierarchical-mesh \
  --max-agents 25 \
  --strategy specialized

                                        Small Teams (6-8 Agents): Hierarchical

                                        Recommended Configuration

                                        # .aqe/config.yaml
fleet:
  topology: hierarchical
  maxAgents: 8
  strategy: specialized

  # Queen configuration
  queen:
    enabled: true
    workStealingEnabled: true
    consensusAlgorithm: simple-majority

  # Agent allocation
  agents:
    core: 3          # test-gen, coverage, executor
    security: 2      # scanner, auditor
    performance: 1   # profiler
    coordinator: 1   # queen
    reserve: 1       # for burst capacity

  # Domain priorities
  domainPriority:
    - core
    - security
    - performance

                                        Architecture Diagram

                                                 ┌─────────────┐
         │    Queen    │
         │ Coordinator │
         └──────┬──────┘
                │
    ┌───────────┼───────────┐
    │           │           │
┌───┴───┐   ┌───┴───┐   ┌───┴───┐
│ Core  │   │ Sec   │   │ Perf  │
│ Pool  │   │ Pool  │   │ Pool  │
├───────┤   ├───────┤   ├───────┤
│ 3 agents │ 2 agents │ 1 agent│
└───────┘   └───────┘   └───────┘

                                        Key Benefits

                                        • Queen handles coordination overhead
                                        • Work stealing prevents bottlenecks
                                        • Clear domain boundaries

                                        Large Teams (10-15 Agents): Hierarchical-Mesh

                                        Recommended Configuration

                                        # .aqe/config.yaml
fleet:
  topology: hierarchical-mesh
  maxAgents: 15
  strategy: specialized

  # Queen configuration
  queen:
    enabled: true
    workStealingEnabled: true
    consensusAlgorithm: supermajority
    delegationEnabled: true  # Domain leads

  # Domain meshes
  domains:
    core:
      agents: 5
      topology: mesh  # Internal mesh
      lead: true      # Has domain coordinator
    security:
      agents: 3
      topology: mesh
      lead: true
    performance:
      agents: 2
      topology: mesh
      lead: false     # Small enough to skip
    browser:
      agents: 2
      topology: mesh
      lead: false
    chaos:
      agents: 2
      topology: mesh
      lead: false

  # Cross-domain communication
  crossDomain:
    protocol: event-driven
    directHandoffEnabled: true

┌──┴──┐        ┌───┴───┐       ┌──┴──┐

│Mesh │        │ Mesh  │      │Mesh │
│5 ag │        │ 3 ag  │      │6 ag │
└─────┘        └───────┘      └─────┘

                                        Key Benefits

                                        • Domain isolation prevents interference
                                        • Domain leads handle local coordination
                                        • Queen only handles cross-domain
                                        • High fault tolerance

                                        Anti-Drift Configuration

                                        Drift occurs when agents deviate from expected behavior over time. These configurations prevent common drift patterns:

                                        RuleValueReason
                                        Max claims per agent
                                        3
                                        		Prevents hoarding, ensures distribution
                                        Stale claim timeout
                                        15 minutes
                                        		Enables work stealing for stuck tasks
                                        Health check interval
                                        30 seconds
                                        		Detects unresponsive agents quickly
                                        Auto-rebalance threshold
                                        3x load imbalance
                                        		Triggers redistribution when skewed
                                        Consensus timeout
                                        5 minutes
                                        		Prevents decision paralysis
                                        Memory cleanup interval
                                        1 hour
                                        		Prevents memory bloat

                                        Complete Anti-Drift Config

                                        # .aqe/config.yaml - Anti-Drift Settings
antiDrift:
  enabled: true

  claims:
    maxPerAgent: 3
    staleTimeoutMinutes: 15
    autoRelease: true

  health:
    checkIntervalSeconds: 30
    unhealthyThreshold: 3        # Consecutive failures
    autoRestart: true

  rebalance:
    loadImbalanceRatio: 3.0
    checkIntervalMinutes: 5
    enabled: true

  consensus:
    timeoutMinutes: 5
    fallbackToQueen: true        # Queen decides if timeout

  memory:
    cleanupIntervalMinutes: 60
    maxPatternsPerAgent: 1000

  monitoring:
    metricsEnabled: true
    alertOnDrift: true
    slackWebhook: ${SLACK_WEBHOOK}

                                        Quick Start Commands

                                        Small Team (Hierarchical)

                                        # Initialize
npx @claude-flow/cli@latest swarm init \
  --topology hierarchical \
  --max-agents 8 \
  --strategy specialized

# Spawn workers
aqe hive-mind spawn --count 6 --role worker
aqe hive-mind spawn --count 1 --role specialist

                                        Large Team (Hierarchical-Mesh)

                                        # Initialize
npx @claude-flow/cli@latest swarm init \
  --topology hierarchical-mesh \
  --max-agents 15 \
  --strategy specialized

# Spawn domain workers
aqe hive-mind spawn --count 5 --role worker --domain core
aqe hive-mind spawn --count 3 --role worker --domain security
aqe hive-mind spawn --count 4 --role worker --domain mixed

                                        Scaling Guide

                                        When to Scale Up

                                        • - Agent utilization consistently > 80%
                                        • - Task queue depth growing
                                        • - Response times increasing
                                        • - Work stealing happening frequently

                                        When to Scale Down

                                        • - Agent utilization consistently < 30%
                                        • - Many idle agents
                                        • - Memory pressure increasing
                                        • - Cost optimization needed
                                        # Dynamic scaling
aqe agent pool scale --target-size 10   # Scale to 10 agents
aqe agent pool status                    # Check current pool
aqe agent pool drain --type idle         # Remove idle agents
